title: Meety Bourguignon
notes: Seitan. Seitan is a meat replacement that loosely translated from Japanese means “made of proteins”. It’s also called wheat protein, wheat meat or wheat gluten. It is processed from wheat flour and has a meat-like texture and neutral flavour but absorbs other flavours well. Store-bought versions can be high in sodium and, obviously, if you have any issues digesting gluten you should stay away from it. While it is a good source of protein, it lacks many amino acids and other essential nutrients and is not concidered a complete protein, therefore it needs to be considered as only one part of a balanced diet. It is, however, low in calories, a soy-free meat replacement and very versatile.

ingredientSections.heading: Protein Options
items: ¾ Cup water or vegetable broth
Optional: extra soy sauce or tamari, onion, fresh ginger

methodSections.heading: Stew Base
steps: Slice the onion then sautée with the garlic together in a large pot until soft.
Chop the carrots into 1cm (½in) disks and add to the pot along with the wine, rosemary, thyme, paprika, tomato paste, salt and pepper. Bring to a boil and let the wine reduce by half.
Dissolve the bouillon in 3 cups of hot water to form a broth. Add the porcinis and broth to the pot and bring back to a boil for 5 minutes.
Cut the potatoes into a large dice and add to the pot. Lower the heat and simmer for about 15 minutes until potatoes are tender.

In a small bowl stir together the rice flour and half a cup water until smooth. Temper mixture by adding spoonfuls of hot broth until similar in temperature. Then slowly pour into pot mixing well. Let the stew thicken for around 5 minutes and then add your protein of choice from the options below.

methodSections.heading: Protein Options
steps: For Soy Curls (T.V.P.): Rehydrate in warm water as directed until tender. Squeeze out any excess water.
In a separate bowl create a seasoning mix by combining the onion and garlic powder and paprika. Season to taste.
Toss soy curls in the seasoning and then sautée in a frying pan with the oil until curls start to crust. Add to the stew and stir.
For Vegan Sausages: Cut into 2cm (1in) discs and add to stew. You could also brown the sausages in a frying pan before adding to the stew.
For Store-Bought Seitan: Slice before searing in a hot pan with a little oil. When the stew is ready to serve, add the seitan. If the seitan is cooked further in the stew it could turn rubbery.
For Homemade Seitan: Combine the gluten, dry spices, soy sauce and broth into a dough. Knead several times, allow to sit for 5-10 minutes and then knead a few more times.

Divide the dough into thirds and shape as desired. Bring the broth and optional additional flavourings to a slow simmer and boil the seitan for an hour. Follow the store-bought seitan instructions, above, before adding to the stew.
